I am old now, seventy-six years, and this small piece of land near my house is just a little plot where I grow what I can to eat. I have no money for the fertilizer from the shop — that costs too much for such a small piece, and the bag is too big anyway. I will put the manure from my few chickens and what sweepings I have from the cooking place, and I will use the seeds I saved from last harvest like my mother taught me. My hands are slow now but I can still weed and plant myself, with maybe my granddaughter helping me some days.
